The present application is filed by the applicants under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for quashing the impugned FIR being C.R. No.11210031200106 of 2020 registered before the Mahila Police Station, Surat City for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323,
504, 114 and 506(2) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
1.2 The learned advocate for the applicants does not press this application qua the applicants No.1 and 2 only.
Therefore, the present application is disposed of as not pressed qua the applicants No.1 and 2 only.
For applicants No.3 to 5, this application is heard and decided today with NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/239/2021 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined the consent of all the learned advocates.

2. 3. Heard learned advocates. Rule.
Learned APP and learned advocate Mr.Minhaj Shaikh waive service of notice of rule on behalf of the respective respondents.
4. Learned advocate for the applicant Mr.Samir Afzal Khan has submitted that the complainant remarried with another boy and is at present pregnant.

He has submitted that before the trial Court,
the complainant has withdrawn the complaint under the Dowry Act against all the applicants.
He has submitted that the complainant has also withdrawn the complaint for maintenance under Section 125 from the learned trial Court.
He has submitted that without getting divorce, the complainant got remarried with another boy.

He has submitted that on one hand, the complainant got remarried with another boy and on the another hand, the complainant is contesting this application before this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/239/2021 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined
He has submitted that even otherwise, except the general and vague allegations, no offence is made out against the applicants.
He has submitted that the complainant resided with the applicants for only 15 days and thereafter, she was residing separate along with her husband.
He has submitted that both the sisters-in-law are married and residing in her matrimonial homes.
He has submitted that this is a case of over implication as the whole family members are dragged into the offence in question.
He has submitted that the impugned complaint is made after much delay.
He has submitted that this application may be allowed.
5. Per contra, learned advocate Mr.Shaikh for the original complainant has submitted that there is prima facie offence made out against the applicants.
He has submitted that the applicants have tortured the complainant mentally and physical lot during her marriage span.
He has submitted that the in-laws has tortured the complainant by demanding dowry of Rs.5 lakhs.
He has submitted that though the sisters-in-law are residing separately, they often visited their parental homes and thereby tried to disturb the marriage life of the complainant.
He has fairly submitted that the complainant got remarried with another boy and is pregnant.
He has submitted that this application may be rejected.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/239/2021 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined 6.
Learned APP for the State has submitted that it is a matrimonial dispute between the parties.
He has submitted that the complainant got remarried with another boy.
He has submitted looking to the entire circumstances of the case, appropriate order may be passed.
7. I have heard rival submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties.
I have perused the documents available on record.
From record, the following factors are emerged before this Court for consideration of this application.
The complaint is lodged after much delay of about more than 10 months.

sentences.text: The allegations are general in nature.
The complainant got remarried with another boy and is pregnant.
There is no divorce between the complainant and applicant No.1 - husband.
The complainant resided for 15 days only at her matrimonial home.
The complainant and her husband was residing separately.
The other in-laws were not residing with the complainant.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/239/2021 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined  The sisters-in-law are married and settled at their matrimonial homes.
The mother-in-law is aged lady.
The complainant has withdrawn maintenance proceedings against the husband.
The complainant has also withdrawn the complaint under the Dowry Act.
On one hand, the complainant got remarried with another boy without divorce and is pregnant and on the other hand, she is contesting this application before this Court.
This is an abuse of process of law by the complainant.

8. Further, it will be fruitful to mention the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana V/s Bhajan Lal reported in AIR 1992 SC 604, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed thus - "In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Ch.XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Art.226 or the inherent powers under sec.482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/239/2021 ORDER DATED:
20/07/2023 undefined be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised.

sentences.text: (1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

sentences.text:
(2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under sec.156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of sec.155(2) of the Code.

(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/239/2021 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined sec.156(2)
of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

(7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
9. Looking to the entire facts and circumstances of the case, this is a gross case of abuse of process of law by the complainant.
On one hand, the complainant got remarried with another boy and is pregnant, without divorce and on the other hand, the complainant is contesting this application before this Court.

Further, the complainant has withdrawn NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/239/2021 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined the case of maintenance before the learned trial against the applicants as well as also withdrawn the dowry proceedings.

This is a fit case to exercise the powers by this Court in favour of the applicants under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1908.
10.
For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
10.1 The present application is allowed qua the applicants No.3 to 5 only.
